title: Redwood discovery - Quasar Finance latency & throughput
summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency targets for real-time fraud scoring, expected concurrency (~200 rps peak), streaming requirements for progressive scoring, and token/sec benchmarking. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, security (SOC2, KMS, VPC) and next steps: run benchmarks on sample prompt set, share pricing and security docs, and scope Dedicated sizing for POC.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
next_steps: Alex to send pricing deck and Dedicated sizing template (due 2027-10-15)
Priya to share benchmark script and test configs; run initial token/sec test with Quasar prompts (target by 2027-10-20)
Quasar to share sample prompt set + success criteria for p95 latency (Anika to deliver by 2027-10-17)
Schedule POC scoping call with Quasar infra + security (tentative 2027-10-22)
action_items: Priya Nair (SE): prepare benchmark script and test config (due 2027-10-20)
Alex Chen (AE): send pricing + contract template (due 2027-10-15)
Anika Bose (Quasar): share sample prompts and traffic profile (due 2027-10-17)
Jared Kim (Quasar Infra): provide VPC/network constraints and required egress rules (due 2027-10-18)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Alex from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. Uh, can you all introduce quickly?
[00:07] Michael Torres: Yeah hi I'm Michael, CTO at Quasar. We run real-time fraud scoring across payments and loans.
[00:11] Anika Bose: Anika, lead ML engineer, I'll own the model side and the prompt set.
[00:14] Jared Kim: Jared, infra, I look after networking and deployments.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: we want to surface p95 and p99 latency targets, concurrency needs, streaming early-token scoring, and how best to run token/sec benchmarks — also map Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for your security needs. Sound good?
[00:28] Michael: Yes, exactly. To start — our hard requirement is p95 under 150ms for the inline fraud scoring path. That is non-negotiable for checkout flows.
[00:36] Alex: Got it. p95 150ms, can I ask what's the payload? Average prompt length, typical tokens?
[00:41] Anika: Our prompts are compact — about 60 to 120 tokens average, with a few long-tail cases up to 400 tokens when we include enriched context.
[00:49] Jared: Concurrency — at peak we see ~200 requests per second to the fraud model, spikes up to 350 for promos.
[00:55] Priya: Ok so that's pretty sizeable. Two follow-ups — are you planning synchronous scoring in the user flow (blocking), or async? And do you need streaming partial outputs to make early decisions?
[01:04] Michael: Blocking path, low latency is critical. We may want streaming for some longer contexts to start taking action before full completion.
[01:12] Anika: We also want token/sec benchmarking because our decision logic sometimes relies on partial tokens — so throughput matters for batch offline scoring as well.
[01:20] Alex: Understood. For Hosted (our default) we provide multi-tenant endpoints with strong latency, but Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and consistent throughput which helps hitting p95s at scale. Private adds VPC/on-prem where we can swap in customer-managed KMS and tighter network controls.
[01:33] Jared: Network-wise we prefer VPC peering; can't expose PII outside our VPC. Is that supported with Private only? Or can Dedicated do VPC?
[01:41] Priya: Dedicated supports private networking options — we can do VPC peering and private link with dedicated capacity. Private (on-prem / VPC-managed) is for more locked-down setups. There are tradeoffs: Hosted gets you fastest onboarding, Dedicated gives predictable latency and SLOs, Private gives full control but adds ops overhead.
[01:56] Michael: Latency — what's realistic for p95 with 60-120 tokens on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[02:02] Priya: Ballpark: for a compact decoder-only model on GPU-C+ class hardware, Hosted p95 in a multi-tenant env could be around 120-180ms depending on bursts and batching. Dedicated with reserved capacity reduces tail and jitter — we often see p95 closer to 90-130ms for that token range. Private depends on infra but you can hit similar numbers if you provide comparable GPUs and network.
[02:25] Anika: We're also using kv cache and prefix caching — how does that affect tokens/sec? I heard Redwood has KV cache optimizations.
[02:32] Priya: Yes, we do prefix and KV cache. That reduces repeated compute for similar context (like customer history). That helps bring per-request compute down significantly for long sessions. Note: transcription may say k v cash sometimes — people hear cash — but it's KV cache.
[02:45] Michael: For our benchmarks, we need token/sec and tokens per GPU metrics. Do you have a standard benchmark harness?
[02:52] Priya: We'll provide a benchmark script — it's in the deck and also we can run it for you. It measures end-to-end latency (client to response), tokens/sec, and GPU utilization over defined prompts, and supports streaming measurement (first-token latency, and time-to-n tokens). We'll share a spreadsheet.
[03:08] Alex: We'll also include an example config for batch sizes, concurrent requests, and sequence lengths.
[03:13] Jared: Another point — TLS termination, KMS, and audit logs. We need SOC2 plus ability to rotate keys via our KMS.
[03:20] Priya: We support KMS integrations and audit logs; Dedicated and Private give you more control over key management and audit retention. Hosted is SOC2 compliant and you get standard audit trails. We'll attach the security pack link afterwards.
[03:32] Michael: Great. Pricing sensitivity — Dedicated reserved capacity is something we can buy, but we need clear math on cost per token after batching/kv and for streaming.
[03:40] Alex: We'll send a pricing deck with worked examples showing with and without caching, different batch sizes, and the cost per p95 improvement tradeoff.
[03:47] Anika: For the token/sec benchmark — we often see models degrade under concurrency: tail latency jumps. How do you handle autoscale and fallbacks?
[03:55] Priya: The runtime has autoscaling policies and can fallback to a compatible model variant or a quantized profile when capacity is constrained. We also have smart routing by region and tier to reduce cross-traffic. For p95-sensitive endpoints we'd recommend Dedicated with canary rollouts and autoscale thresholds tuned to keep tail low.
[04:12] Michael: If we need streaming and first-token under 50ms is required for a partial decision, is that feasible?
[04:18] Priya: First-token latencies are often network + model compute. With Dedicated and optimized kernels, for small contexts you can get first-token in ~30-60ms on good hardware. But it depends on model architecture, quantization, and sequence handling. We'll need to test with your exact model/config.
[04:33] Jared: About the model — are we running our own finetuned model or one of Redwood's catalog models? We plan to use an internal, fine-tuned variant.
[04:39] Alex: Both are supported. For private models we can host the artifact in your registry or in our managed model store with versioning. For Dedicated we do pinned versions per pool. For security we can restrict image access and use customer-managed keys for artifacts in Private.
[04:55] Anika: Ok let's talk metrics for the benchmark. We want p50, p95, p99, average tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and a streaming-first-token profile. Also error rates under load.
[05:06] Priya: Sounds good. We'll instrument the harness to capture those. We'll recommend a load shape: steady at 200 rps, 10-minute sustained window, plus spike tests to 350 rps, and also some long-tail sequences to 400 tokens to see tail behavior.
[05:18] Michael: That matches our traffic. Can you also simulate traffic with prefix cache hits vs cold cache to see the delta?
[05:24] Priya: Absolutely — we can include cache-hit ratios (0%, 50%, 80%) in the spreadsheet. That usually shows large wins for long sessions.
[05:32] Alex: About SLAs — Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency targets and uptime. We can propose p95 SLOs as part of a contract for the POC.
[05:40] Jared: For VPC peering, what egress ports are required? We need the exact network policy so we can run it by our security team.
[05:47] Priya: We'll include a network checklist in the security pack, covering ports, allowed CIDRs, and cert thumbprint info.
[05:54] Anika: Any gotchas around streaming in Dedicated vs Hosted? We had issues in the past where the multi-tenant env batched streams and introduced micro-bursts.
[06:02] Priya: Good point. Hosted may batch more aggressively for efficiency which can slightly increase tail for streaming-first-token. Dedicated can be tuned with smaller batch windows and reserved capacity to keep streaming latency predictable. Also kernel selection and quantization profiles matter.
[06:16] Michael: On the topic of quantization — if we apply int8 or other quant profiles for speed, how much regression in model quality should we expect? We need to keep false positive/negative rates low.
[06:25] Priya: Quality impact depends on model and task. We recommend running quality regressions tied to eval sets; Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles with expected quality deltas. For fraud scoring, we typically avoid aggressive quant if it materially affects metrics; sometimes we do mixed profiles where high-risk paths use full precision.
[06:40] Alex: We'll include a suggested eval plan: A/B test on the scoring metric and ROC curves for any quantized variant.
[06:45] Jared: Contractually, we need to know data residency and retention for logs.
[06:50] Priya: We can set log retention and data deletion policies; Dedicated/Private give you stronger guarantees and audit controls. Hosted is configurable but more standardized.
[06:59] Anika: Ok, operationally — can we get a small smoke test POC for a week with dedicated pool? We want to run the benchmark and a few live samples.
[07:07] Alex: Yes we can propose a 2-week POC: one week of benchmark + config tuning, second week of shadow/live integration. We'll size a small Dedicated pool to meet the 200 rps target with headroom.
[07:17] Michael: Cost-wise can you give a rough delta vs Hosted? I understand it varies but we need a decision threshold.
[07:23] Alex: We'll put together sample calculations in the pricing deck: cost per hour for reserved GPUs, expected tokens/sec and resulting cost per 1M tokens, and show how caching and batching reduce the effective cost.
[07:33] Anika: For the benchmark harness, Priya — can you also surface per-request breakdown (network, queuing, compute)? We've seen queuing spikes on our infra that look like network but turned out to be batching.
[07:41] Priya: Yes we'll capture client-to-gateway latency, queue time inside the runtime, and model compute time. We'll also include kernel/heavy op breakdown where possible.
[07:50] Jared: On the security front, we may need a joint call with our security team. Can we schedule that after you send the security pack?
[07:56] Alex: Absolutely. We'll send the security docs and propose times for a security deep-dive.
[08:01] Michael: Good. Any other technical constraints we should tell you now?
[08:04] Anika: We need SAML SSO and RBAC for model access, and audit logs for inference requests tied to user IDs.
[08:10] Priya: We support SAML and RBAC. For inference-level audit logs we can instrument tokens and trace IDs — in Dedicated/Private you can retain logs for longer.
[08:19] Alex: Ok let's recap next steps...
[08:21] Alex: Action items — Alex send pricing deck, Priya share benchmark harness, Quasar to share prompts and infra constraints, and schedule security review.
[08:30] Michael: That all sounds good. Thanks, we'll get the prompts and traffic profiles to you.
[08:34] Alex: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the links and proposed POC dates.
[08:38] [call ends]
